lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's do pricing today. I want a number we can actually defend to somebody.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five dollars a month. I've thought about it and I don't think we should overthink it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five a month. Why five specifically?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's under the line where anyone stops to think about it. It's coffee money.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: People will obviously pay monthly for something they open every single day. So five is fine, and we build the whole thing around the subscription.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. So then the only question is how many we need.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two thousand subscribers and we're both covered. That's the whole business plan on one line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two thousand out of how many people who try it, though?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Call it three percent converting. So we need something like seventy thousand installs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Seventy thousand. Okay. That's a real marketing problem, not a pricing problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which is kind of a relief, honestly. Marketing problems you can attack.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's talk about what's inside the subscription then. What's free and what isn't?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My instinct is the first few photos are free, forever, no account needed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many is a few?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three a week? Enough to get the feeling, not enough to live on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three a week is generous. I'd have said three total.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three total and you never learn whether it works on your actual fridge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair. Let's start generous and tighten it if the costs bite.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Agreed. And the paid tier is unlimited photos plus the leftover tracking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leftover tracking being the thing nobody else does well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the bit I'd pay for myself, which is usually a decent sign.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Alright. Five dollars, three free photos a week, leftovers behind the wall.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Write it down and let's look at it again after the prototype.

moments.description: B picks five dollars a month (line 1) and at line 4 A asserts that people will obviously pay monthly for a daily app, then builds the whole revenue plan on that. Nobody asks whether a cooking utility is a subscription people keep, and the plan is never tested.
